question: A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of a painless lump on her neck. Examination shows a hard nodule on the left side of her neck. A fine-needle aspiration biopsy shows well-differentiated cuboidal cells arranged spherically around colloid. She undergoes thyroidectomy. Histopathological examination of the surgical specimen shows invasion of the thyroid capsule and blood vessels. Which of the following cellular events is most likely involved in the pathogenesis of this patient's condition?

options.opb: Activation mutation in the BRAF gene

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thyroid nodule" -> "Fine-needle aspiration biopsy shows cuboidal cells around colloid" -> "Thyroidectomy performed" -> "Histopathological examination shows invasion of thyroid capsule and blood vessels" -> "Mutation in the RET proto-oncogene" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Thyroid nodule" -> "Fine-needle aspiration biopsy shows cuboidal cells around colloid" -> "Thyroidectomy performed" -> "Histopathological examination shows invasion of thyroid capsule and blood vessels" -> "Activation mutation in the BRAF gene" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with a painless lump on the neck, along with the histopathological findings of invasion of the thyroid capsule and blood vessels, is indicative of thyroid cancer. The presence of well-differentiated cuboidal cells arranged spherically around colloid suggests papillary thyroid carcinoma, which is commonly associated with mutations in the RET proto-oncogene.
